{"success": true, "doc_name": "LACERS__2025_actuarial_consulting_services_rfp.pdf", "structure": [{"title": "February 7, 2025", "node_id": "0000", "start_index": 1, "end_index": 2, "summary": "LACERS RFP No. 4282 seeks actuarial consulting services. Released January 24, 2025, proposals are due electronically February 21, 2025. Julie Guan is the RFP Administrator. Written questions are due by February 7 and must be sent to her; questions and answers, and any official addenda, will be posted on the LACERS website. Proposers are responsible for monitoring the site and following addenda. From release until contract execution, firms may communicate about the RFP only with the Administrator; prohibited contact with Board members or other staff may result in disqualification under LACERS’ ethics policy. The RFP covers introduction, minimum qualifications, consulting/advisory and as-needed services, response contents (introduction, qualifications and experience, project proposal, and actuary fee schedule), submission instructions and evaluation, general conditions and compliance documents, and Executive Directive 35."}, {"title": "I. INTRODUCTION", "node_id": "0001", "start_index": 3, "end_index": 4, "summary": "LACERS seeks proposals from qualified public-pension actuarial consultants meeting Section II qualifications. It plans a full-service three-year Consulting Actuary contract, with up to two one-year extensions. The consultant must serve LACERS and its members exclusively, may serve the City only at LACERS’ request, and must cooperate with any City-appointed actuary or auditor by supplying requested data. Established in 1937, LACERS covers about 25,200 active employees and 22,500 retirees and beneficiaries, paying roughly $1.21 billion in pensions and $174 million in retiree-health premiums annually. Its seven-member Board governs the system; benefits are set by the City, with Tier 1 (including Enhanced) and Tier 3 memberships. LACERS administers a defined-benefit retirement plan, postemployment health plan (401(h) and 115 Trust), Larger Annuity Plan, and Family Death Benefit Plan. The RFP directs proposers to online valuations, audits, studies, policies, financial reports, and Board materials and lists relevant meeting dates. A separate future RFP may select an Audit Actuary to review assumptions and validate valuations."}, {"title": "II. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS", "node_id": "0002", "start_index": 4, "end_index": 4, "summary": "Firms must demonstrate these minimum qualifications to be considered: at least five years providing comparable actuarial consulting services to U.S. public pension funds; a supervising/lead actuary with at least 15 years’ experience with major public employee retirement systems, including three years serving California public pension clients similar to LACERS in size and services. The lead actuary must meet American Academy of Actuaries qualification standards, hold an SOA Fellow or Associate designation or equivalent, directly supervise all LACERS services, and be an employee regularly engaged in actuarial services.
